newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia to boost 1997 titanium exports by quarter.
newsitem.headline: Russia to boost 1997 titanium exports by quarter.

text.p: Russia, the world's largest titanium producer, hopes to boost exports of the metal by more than a quarter this year as domestic demand continues to stagnate, a Russian industry official said on Thursday.

Yury Yurkov, a manager of Verkhnaya Salda Metallurgical Production Association (VSMPO), told a meeting of Japanese titanium users that it hopes to sell 9,000 tonnes of titanium worldwide this year against 7,100 tonnes last year.
VSMPO, now a joint stock company which produces 95 percent of Russia's titanium, would make 11,000 tonnes of the metal and its alloy in 1997, up 15.8 percent from 9,500 tonnes in 1996, he said.
Yet output remains minimal compared to annual production of 100,000 tonnes before the end of the Cold War, when the Soviet arms industry swallowed a huge quantity of the rare metal.
Yurkov said Russia's annual domestic demand had stagnated at around 2,000 tonnes in recent years.
VSMPO, which sold titanium abroad for the first time in 1992, is now on an export drive, seeking civilian applications for the light, strong, corrosion-resistant metal.
The association is raising titanium alloy ingot output to meet growing demand from the U.S. and European aerospace industries, though most of its 60,000-tonne production capacity remains idle.

Yurkov, on a two-week trip to Japan, said VSMPO hoped to boost exports to the country. Russian's exports to Japan dived to 360 tonnes in 1996 from 900 tonnes the previous year due to an unfavourable foreign exchange rate.
VSMPO had already emerged as Boeing Co's largest titanium provider and as one of the main suppliers to Airbus Industrie, he said.
In 1996, some 60 percent of VSMPO's titanium exports went to the United States, about a quarter to western Europe, 10 percent to Taiwan and only five percent to Japan.
"We have started very seriously to work out a strategy for Japan," he said, adding that Japan was very attractive as it has many different civilian uses for titanium.
Asked about possible Russian government stockpile sales of titanium sponge, Yurkov said: "It is very interesting. We are considering buying it."

The VSMPO official said he had no details of the latest government offer but in 1995 VSMPO exchanged about 4,000 tonnes of titanium ingot for 4,000 tonnes of titanium sponge from the government stock.
